key_insight: Combining an incident-aware Spatio-Temporal Transformer with Adaptive Conformal Prediction yields accurate, calibrated multi-horizon traffic forecasts that remain robust to intermittent incidents and time-varying spatial dependencies.
problem_solved: Produces reliable long-horizon traffic forecasts under stochastic network conditions and intermittent incidents while providing calibrated uncertainty estimates for safer decision-making.
method: Spatio-Temporal Transformer (STT) that models dynamic spatial dependencies and temporal patterns from ODOT traffic counts.
Incident-awareness: fuse crash/incident records as external inputs to capture disruption effects on flows.
Adaptive Conformal Prediction (ACP) applied to STT outputs to produce calibrated prediction intervals across multiple forecast horizons.
impact: Enables ML practitioners and transportation operators to deploy uncertainty-aware, long-horizon traffic forecasting models that improve reliability, risk assessment, and operational decision-making under disruptive events.
visual_elements: Model architecture diagram showing STT backbone + incident input stream + ACP calibration module
Map of sensor network with incidents overlaid and multi-horizon forecast ribbons per location
Calibration/reliability plot (predicted interval vs empirical coverage) across forecast horizons
Before/after example timeline showing an incident, model forecast, and calibrated uncertainty bands
paper_title: Long-Horizon Traffic Forecasting via Incident-Aware Conformal Spatio-Temporal Transformers
paper_authors: Mayur Patil, Qadeer Ahmed, Shawn Midlam-Mohler, Stephanie Marik, Allen Sheldon
